name: Kwality Wall's (India) Ltd (KWIL)
tagline: India's first standalone listed ice-cream company - demerged from Hindustan Unilever (effective 1 Dec 2025, listed 16 Feb 2026) - but revenue is falling (-30% YoY) and losses are widening in its first quarters as an independent entity.
business_overview: Kwality Wall's (India) Ltd was carved out of HUL's ice-cream business (Wall's, Cornetto, Magnum, Feast) via NCLT-approved demerger, 1:1 share entitlement to HUL shareholders, listing 16 Feb 2026 at ~26% discount to adjusted parent price. The ice-cream business was only ~3% of HUL's pre-demerger revenue (~Rs 1,800 Cr). Seeded via untrusted X triage (@ashwinidamani, 2026-09-13); confirmed as the correct listed entity (NSE/BSE scrip 544622, ticker KWIL) via web search on the HUL demerger.
fundamentals_table: Loss before exceptional items widened to Rs 109.22 Cr (Q3 FY26) vs Rs 97 Cr loss YoY
Demerger effective 1-Dec-2025; listed 16-Feb-2026 at ~26% discount to adjusted HUL price
fundamentals_narrative: As a newly independent entity, KWIL is absorbing standalone costs (distribution network build-out separate from HUL's, brand-licensing/transition costs, working-capital reset) that a captive divisional business never had to bear on its own P&L. Revenue has fallen sharply (-30% YoY in Q3 FY26) and losses have widened rather than narrowed in its first reported quarters post-listing - the opposite of what a clean, well-executed spin-off would show this early. No sign yet of the standalone cost base stabilising.
technical_read: Trading near the lower half of its short post-listing 52-week range (Rs 22.24 - Rs 50.68); not evaluated further given the fundamentals disposition below.
sentiment_summary: No forum deep-dive performed - four-box score is low (1.0) and this is a fast-track large-recognisable-brand disposition, not a promising small-cap lead. topic_id remains null; not resolved this pass.
bse_notes: No red flags found (no CIRP/negative net worth, no SEBI/fraud action, no promoter-pledge or auditor-resignation signal surfaced). Disposition is fundamentals-driven (revenue decline + widening losses), not a red-flag exclusion.
bull_case: Strong recognised brand portfolio (Wall's, Cornetto, Magnum, Feast) with decades of India distribution history
India ice-cream category has long-run premiumisation/per-capita-consumption tailwinds
Now a focused, independent management team free of competing capital-allocation priorities inside a much larger FMCG conglomerate
bear_case: Revenue down 30% YoY and losses widening in the first reported quarters as a standalone company - a difficult separation, not a clean spin-off
Must rebuild distribution/cold-chain infrastructure independently of HUL's much larger general-trade network - a genuine execution risk, not yet proven out
Negative P/E; no visible profitability inflection yet

No specific named management/structural catalyst (new CEO turnaround, capital-allocation regime change) found beyond the demerger itself, which so far reads as value-destructive rather than value-unlocking
market_cap_tier: Mid-cap (~Rs 11,360 Cr), newly listed FMCG spin-off
